Account summary:
- Product: mid-market analytics platform for customer engagement + in-app help widgets. Heavy search + support automation usage.
- Current stack: full product uses OpenAI endpoints (davinci/gpt-4) for chat + a bespoke reranking layer. Considering Redwood to reduce per-token cost and get predictable dedicated capacity.
- Motivation: lower unit costs at scale, stronger routing & caching, and enterprise controls (KMS + audit logs).

POC scope and technical asks:
- Two-phase plan: 1) Hosted API parity validation (2-week regression POC), 2) Move to Dedicated for steady throughput (reserve 4 GPUs initially).
- Key metrics: prompt parity (>97% pass on semantic-sim tests), no >5% negative regressions in user-sentiment triggers, p95 latency target <400ms for 2k-token sessions, sustained throughput 12 reqs/s with batched bursts to 50 reqs/s.
- Migration concerns: prompt formatting differences, tokenization mismatches, model-id mapping (need compat layer for existing SDK calls), function-calling differences. Team quote: "We need to be able to drop-in with minimal prompt surgery — business can't accept a downgrade in NPS."

- Latency: hosted p50/p95 numbers look fine for baseline; dedicated expected to reduce p95 by ~30-40% in model tests.
- Cost: projected 20-35% cost savings vs current OpenAI per-token rates when using batching + prefix caching.
